question.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -4 \\ -26\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -4 \\ -26\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ -4 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}11 & 0 \\ 0 & 18\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ -4 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{198}[\begin{aligned}18 & 0 \\ 0 & 11\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ -4 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{198}[\begin{aligned}18 & 0 \\ 0 & 11\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
